transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because my mind keeps going blank at really bad times. Like, I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms, or even holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. It’s been scaring me.
Do these blank moments seem to happen when you're under a lot of stress or pressure?

Yes, it does feel worse when there’s pressure. Like if I’m looking at the road-closure forms or I’ve got the stop-slow paddle in my hand, my mind just goes blank, and I suddenly can’t remember steps I’ve done for years. That’s what scares me.
Do these blank moments and memory losses last for a while after the pressure or stress is gone?

It can last a bit, yeah. Even after the pressure eases, I’m still kind of stuck, like my mind hasn’t caught up. I’ll be looking at the forms or the paddle and I just can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years, and it takes me a while to feel clear again.
Are you experiencing these memory blanks or difficulties recalling familiar information in situations outside of your job as well?

Mostly I notice it at work. That’s where it really scares me—like I’ll look at the road-closure forms or be holding the stop-slow paddle, and I suddenly can’t remember steps I’ve done for years. Outside of work, I’m not as sure, but the big blank moments are happening there.
Do you feel anxious or overwhelmed in situations outside of your job?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do get stressed outside work sometimes, like anyone, but I haven’t noticed the same kind of overwhelming feeling the way I do at work. It’s harder for me to say.
Do you feel anxious when you're not at work?
Not really that I can clearly say. I mean, I get tense sometimes when I’m not working, but I haven’t noticed that same anxious, overwhelmed feeling the way it happens at work.
Do you ever feel anxious when you're not working?
I don’t really think so. I mean, I can get uneasy here and there, but I haven’t noticed it being a regular thing when I’m not working.
Have you noticed any other problems with your body, like numbness, weakness, or difficulty with coordination?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed numbness or weakness, and I’m not aware of any coordination problems.
Do you ever feel like you're outside of your body watching yourself when these blank moments happen?
No, I don’t think so. I wouldn’t describe it like I’m outside my body watching myself. It’s more just… blank, like I lose track for a bit.
Do you ever feel disconnected from yourself or your surroundings when these blank moments are not happening?
Not that I’ve noticed. I mean, outside of those blank times, I usually feel like I’m just here and aware of what’s around me. I don’t really feel disconnected like that.
Have these memory blanks affected your relationships or daily activities outside of your job?

Yes. It’s been a problem. I wasn’t reliable at work anymore because I couldn’t finish the road-closure paperwork, and I didn’t trust myself with the traffic-safety steps.

Outside of work, I pulled back from things too. I stopped going to choir and volunteering, and I wasn’t really keeping up with family. It got bad enough that they felt like they had to bring me in for help.
Do you ever feel like you're in a daze or spaced out when you're not having one of these blank moments?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I usually feel spaced out unless one of those blank moments is happening. Most of the time I feel pretty aware of where I am.
Do you ever feel like you're not yourself or like things aren't real when you're not having one of those blank moments?
No, I don’t think so. I haven’t really had that feeling like I’m not myself or that things aren’t real, at least not that I’ve noticed. Outside of the blanks, things feel normal in that way.
Do you feel like you're disconnected from your thoughts or feelings when you're not at work?
I’m not sure I’d put it that way. When I’m not at work, I don’t really notice feeling cut off from my thoughts or feelings. I might be quiet or not very motivated, but not disconnected exactly.
Do you have trouble remembering things like appointments, birthdays, or what you did yesterday when you're not at work?

Not so much things like birthdays or what I did yesterday. It’s more like my mind goes blank right when I need it not to. Like I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms, or holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years.
Have you felt like your memory blanks or difficulties have significantly affected your personal relationships or daily life outside of your job?

Yes. It’s mostly affected work, but it spilled over into everything. I stopped being reliable because I couldn’t finish the road-closure paperwork or trust myself with the traffic-safety steps anymore.

And outside work, I kind of pulled back from people. I stopped going to choir, stopped volunteering, and I wasn’t really showing up for my family like I used to. It got bad enough that they felt like they had to bring me in for help.
Do you ever feel like you're not connected to your body or surroundings when you're not at work and not under any particular stress?

Not really, no. If I’m just at home or not stressed, I don’t usually feel like I’m outside my body or like the room isn’t real. I might feel tired or withdrawn, but not disconnected from my body or surroundings like that.
Do you ever feel like you're in a dream or things aren't real when you're not at work and not under any particular stress?
No, I don’t think so. When I’m just at home and things are calm, I don’t usually feel like I’m dreaming or like things aren’t real. I might feel off or tired sometimes, but not in that way.
Do you ever feel like you are not yourself or like things are not real when you are not at work and not feeling stressed?
No, not really. I don’t think I get that feeling when I’m not at work or stressed. I might feel tired or kind of shut down, but I don’t usually feel like I’m not myself or like things aren’t real.
Do you think your blank moments are more related to feeling overwhelmed or to something else entirely?

I think it’s more like my mind just goes blank, even with things I know how to do. Like I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms, or holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. It happens at the worst times, and it scares me because it’s stuff that should be automatic.
